# DiscoPoP B24 — everything the minimum/maximum heuristic cannot read was reported as a maximum (a helper function, `hypot`, a division, a copy): the repair and its regression check

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** done

## The question

After the repair of 12 Oct (a minimum or maximum reduction is reported only where the stored value is a call of a minimum or maximum function with the variable as a direct argument and no other argument reading it; otherwise nothing): does DiscoPoP alone give every one of the 44 tsvc_c3, the 9 tsvc_c4 and the 31 other packages the class and the reduction clauses it had, and do exactly the eight unreadable maximum entries of `s293`, `adi` and `lu` disappear from the reduction files?

## Result in one paragraph

Passed (12 Oct): on the 44 tsvc_c3, the 9 tsvc_c4 and the 31 other packages every class (A 10, D 5, R 29 · A 1, R 8 · A 22, R 9), every outcome and every number of kept directives is as in the draws before the repair — 252 no-model trials in three draws; the reduction files changed exactly where predicted (the six maximum entries on the divisions of `polybench/adi`, the one of `polybench/lu`, the copy of `tsvc_c3/s293`) and none holds a `>` or `<` afterwards. One reduction clause differs between the sets of draws: `reduction(+:A)` on `polybench/lu`, offered in one draw of three before and in none after — which of DiscoPoP's two answers a profile gets (B21); twelve fresh profiles on the repaired DiscoPoP give it nine times. Where the repair acts: on a second file of twelve loops the wrong `reduction(max:…)` on a helper function, `hypot`, `fabs` of a difference, a division, a maximum with the variable in both arguments and a copy are gone (the copy loop had been offered as Do-All too); `fmax`/`fmin` with the variable as a direct argument keep their reduction; given up on purpose: a maximum of a maximum and a clamp. Found on the way and entered as B25 (candidate): one of DiscoPoP's own tests fails about one run in ten on the Mac — the same binary gives two profiles.

| 2026-10-12 | plan | **E4, step 3 pre-registered — what one fast refresh saves where the profiling run is long. No model. Written before the run; registered as `e4_refresh_time`.** **What it is** (`tools/refresh_time.py`): for each program, in the configuration of its trial in `t0_11_b24_apps_a` (DiscoPoP alone, the DiscoPoP with B23 and B24 repaired): the unchanged program is profiled in full once; then an edit that changes nothing — one comment line in front of the file under study, so that every line moves by one and every dependence has to be carried over — and five times, in turn, the profile after that edit is made by the fast refresh (`_reprofil_fast`, from the profile before) and by the full re-profile (`_reprofil`), the order alternating. Each is timed as a whole and in its parts — the compile with instrumentation, the instrumented run, the explorer; what remains of a fast refresh is the carrying over — and DiscoPoP's patterns after each are recorded (Do-All and reduction loops with their clauses; task patterns counted). **The programs, fixed:** the three with the longest profiling run in the draws of 12 Oct and PolyBench's longest — medians of the three draws `t0_11_b24_apps_a` to `_c`, read today: `rodinia-3.1/hotspot` run 50.4 s (compile 0.57 s, explorer 73.6 s), `npb/is` 27.8 s (0.56 s, 13.0 s), `burkardt/md` 21.4 s (0.51 s, 11.7 s), `polybench/correlation` 4.37 s (0.21 s, 3.12 s). Eight of the 31 packages outside TSVC have a run over one second; PolyBench's median is 0.11 s. **Read-outs, fixed now:** per program the seconds of a full re-profile and of a fast refresh (median of five, smallest and largest), the difference and the share saved; the parts; in how many of the five the fast refresh was usable; in how many its patterns equal those of the full re-profile beside it; and the five full re-profiles among themselves (on programs where DiscoPoP's answer varies from profile to profile — B21 — a difference from the fast refresh means nothing unless the full profiles agree). **No test:** four programs; the time half of H6 ('the fast refresh saves time') is reported in seconds, and as held on a program if the fast refresh is the shorter one in each of its five pairs. **Expected, written now:** the saving is the instrumented run, less the carrying over — about 50 s, 28 s, 21 s and 4 s, that is about 40 % of one refresh on `hotspot` (whose explorer takes longer than its run), about two thirds on `is` and `md`, a little over half on `correlation`. The carrying over has never been timed on files of this size (it aligns the two lists of instructions as wholes); I expect seconds, and would report it if it eats the saving. The patterns after the fast refresh of an unchanged program are the full profile's wherever the full profiles agree among themselves. **What the archive already says about the share of an agent run** (E1 of September, the agent of that time, arm `default`, five trials each, read today, `history/E01_main_comparison`, runs `e1_r_a` and `e1_r_b`): `md` 1,670 to 2,394 s per trial with 2 to 7 full re-profiles; `is` 1,077 s to the 5,400 s limit with 2 to 7; `hotspot` 683 to 1,372 s with one. So even where the run is long, the runs a fast refresh would skip are 1.5 to 7.7 per cent of a trial (each trial's re-profiles times the run's seconds, over its duration: `md` 2.6 to 6.8 %, `is` 1.5 to 7.7 %, `hotspot` 3.7 to 7.4 %); the read-out gives that share with the measured saving. **Limits, said before the run:** an edit that changes nothing is the most favourable case for the fast refresh's verdict — step 1 measured the unfavourable one, the model's real rewrites, on small loops only; no real rewrite of these four programs is replayed, because the archive holds almost none that passed the checks. One machine, one day. **Where:** the server, one program per 12-core group, about 20 minutes (the longest: `hotspot`, six full profiles of about 125 s and five fast refreshes of about 75 s). | Plan, E4 step 3 pre-registration |

One reduction clause that DiscoPoP offers on `polybench/lu` came in one of three draws before and in none of three after — the all-or-none draw of B21, shown by twelve fresh profiles; the criterion 'no reduction clause differs' is not met as I wrote it for that one package, and I read the regression as passed.** **Runs (all valid, no model):** `t0_11_c3_b24_a`, `t0_11_c3_b24_b`, `t0_11_c3_b24_c`, `t0_11_c4_b24_a`, `t0_11_c4_b24_b`, `t0_11_c4_b24_c`, `t0_11_b24_apps_a`, `t0_11_b24_apps_b`, `t0_11_b24_apps_c` — 252 trials, 0 model calls, 17:16 to 19:15 UTC, every launch after PARITY OK at `4a3de7be8` (the profiler rebuilt on the server from `2c7e95fb3`); sweep clean. **Before the server was touched** (`results/T0_instruments/B24_unreadable_as_max/analysis/mac_checks.md`): the second file of twelve loops — the four loops whose direction can be read keep their reduction, the eight others get nothing (the copy loop loses its Do-All as well); the first file keeps its maximum and three minima and loses `hypot` and `fabs` of a difference; the new end-to-end test passes; the profiler's 184 unit tests and eight feature checks pass; of the 38 end-to-end tests one existing test fails in about one run in ten on the Mac for a reason in the profiler's runtime (B25, below); `s316` with `fmin` is still `min:x`, `s314` with `fmax` still `max:x`. **On the server** (`server_checks.md`, LLVM 20.1.2): both files as on the Mac; all 38 end-to-end tests pass. **The regression** (`analysis/b24_readout.md`, against `t0_11_c3_b23_a` to `_c`, `t0_11_c4_b23_a` to `_c`, `t0_11_b23_apps_a` to `_c`). `tsvc_c3`: A 10, D 5, R 29 before and after; no package with another class, outcome, number of kept directives, offered directive or reduction clause. `tsvc_c4`: A 1, R 8; the same zeros. Outside TSVC: A 22, R 9 before and after; no package with another class, outcome or number of kept directives in any draw; in eight the loops offered differ in some draw, as between any two sets of draws there. **The one difference in reduction clauses:** `polybench/lu`. DiscoPoP gives this kernel one of two answers per profile — `reduction(+:A)` on the loop of line 67 with the outer loop blocked, or the outer loop called parallel and no reduction (B21). The first came in two of three draws on 8 Oct, in one of three in the draws of B23 and in none of the three now. The clause is a sum whose entries in the reduction file the repair does not touch (`+` three times before and after), and the repaired DiscoPoP still produces it: twelve fresh profiles of `lu` on the server give the first answer nine times and the second three times (`analysis/lu_fresh_profiles.txt`). Three draws without it are the coin, not the repair. **The scope check:** 84 reduction files; three changed, exactly the predicted ones — `polybench/adi` loses six maximum entries, `polybench/lu` one, `tsvc_c3/s293` its only entry; no file holds a `>` or a `<` afterwards. **Predicted on 12 Oct and what came:** classes unchanged — yes; reduction clauses unchanged — yes on TSVC, and outside it up to the all-or-none draws that the prediction named; the three files — exactly. **Reading.** Nothing measured in this thesis rested on an entry the heuristic could not read: no class moves and no kept directive changes. From here on DiscoPoP writes a minimum or maximum reduction only for `fmin`/`fmax` with the variable as a direct argument. **Also found, not this repair's doing — B25 (candidate):** one of DiscoPoP's own end-to-end tests (`sharing_clauses/do_all/shared/case_4`) fails in about one run in ten on the Mac because the same instrumented binary sometimes records no `INIT` for a stack array (2 of 24 runs of the test; 3 of 31 runs of one binary; the explorer answers the same on one profile 40 of 40 times); on the server it passes 30 of 30 before and after the repair. Entered in the bug list, not traced. | Result, B24 regression |
| 2026-10-12 | decision | **The author: "ok i agree go ahead" — DiscoPoP B24 is repaired too, and the fast-refresh experiment (E4) runs in the four steps, with the three sentences of the request corrected and the request sent separately after the rewrite. What is fixed before any change.** His message answers the report of 11 Oct, which listed two things as waiting for him, each with my recommendation: B24 ('repair it too? I recommend yes') and the three questions of the design page (the design: the four steps; the three sentences: corrected as shown; the form: a separate request after the rewrite). Read as agreement with all four; his to change. **(1) B24 is wider than I told him, measured before any change** (the installed DiscoPoP with B23 repaired, the Mac, a second file of twelve loops, `b24/repro/mm2.c`, kept with the read-out): the heuristic reports as a maximum every store whose value uses the loaded value of the variable through something that is not an arithmetic the profiler knows — not only a call. Wrong on the file: a helper function that computes a minimum (`x = min2(x, a[i]);`), `hypot`, `fabs` of a difference, a maximum that has the variable in both arguments, a division (`x = x / (2.0 + b[i]);`), and a plain copy of the first element (`b[i] = b[0];`, for which DiscoPoP writes `reduction(max:b)`). Right: `fmax`/`fmin` with the variable as one argument, also with `fabs` in the other argument and through a conversion, and a maximum of a maximum. A clamp (`x = fmin(fmax(x, a[i]), 0.25);`) is reported as a maximum too. The eight maximum entries the regression of B23 found in the benchmark packages are of this kind, read today in the sources: six divisions in `polybench/adi` (lines 81, 85, 94, 98), one in `polybench/lu` (line 65) and the copy `a[i] = a[0];` of `tsvc_c3/s293`; no reduction clause comes of them in any draw. **(2) The repair, as put to him:** a minimum or maximum reduction is reported only where the direction can be read — the stored value, looked at through conversions, is a call of a minimum or maximum function (`fmin`, `fminf`, `fminl`, `fmax`, `fmaxf`, `fmaxl`, the intrinsics `llvm.minnum`, `llvm.minimum`, `llvm.minimumnum`, `llvm.smin`, `llvm.umin` and their maximum twins), the loaded value of the variable is one of its arguments directly or through a conversion, and no other argument reads the variable (checked by the variable's address, since one line may load it twice). In every other case nothing is reported and the loop keeps its carried dependence. **Lost with it, on purpose:** a maximum of a maximum (`x = fmax(fmax(x, a[i]), b[i]);`) and the clamp are no longer reported — a missed chance, never a wrong directive; the rule is not widened for them. No new form is recognised (the `if` and `?:` forms stay as they are; the heuristic's own example from LULESH was never caught and is not caught now). **(3) What can change:** only reductions with the operation `max` whose stored value is not such a call — they disappear. In the archive none of the 25 `max` clauses DiscoPoP wrote is of that kind (all are `fmax`/`fmin` with the variable as a direct argument), and the `s316` re-run's candidates carry four `reduction(min:x)` and no maximum: no trial is run again, and the tables' note on DiscoPoP versions gains a clause, not a version. **(4) Predicted before the server run:** on the 84 packages every class and every reduction clause as in the draws of B23; the reduction files of `s293`, `adi` and `lu` lose their maximum entries (eight) and no file holds a `>` or a `<` afterwards; nothing else differs beyond the known all-or-none draws outside TSVC. **(5) Checked before the server:** both test files before and after; a new end-to-end test with the wrong forms (no reduction and no Do-All on them) and `fmax(x, fabs(a[i]))`; DiscoPoP's end-to-end tests, the profiler's unit tests, the agent's feature checks; `s316` with `fmin` still `min:x`, `s314` with `fmax` still `max:x`. **(6) The regression, registered as group B24 before the first job:** `t0_11_c3_b24_a`, `t0_11_c3_b24_b`, `t0_11_c3_b24_c`, `t0_11_c4_b24_a`, `t0_11_c4_b24_b`, `t0_11_c4_b24_c`, `t0_11_b24_apps_a`, `t0_11_b24_apps_b`, `t0_11_b24_apps_c` — against the draws of B23. Pass: classes and reduction clauses unchanged; scope: reduction files changed exactly where predicted. **(7) E4.** The four steps of the design row of 10 Oct stand as the plan. Step 1 (the replay of the saved rewrites, no model) gets its own pre-registration row and its registration before it runs — on the DiscoPoP with B23 and B24 repaired, after this regression. The three sentences are changed to the wording he was shown, in `_SYSTEM_RECONSTRUCT`, `_RECON_ADDENDUM` and the request of `ask_after_gate`, with the prompt manifest's check naming exactly the arms that carry them; the request is sent separately after the rewrite. No model call before step 2's exact cost has been put to him. | Decision (author), B24 and E4 |
